utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, I heard the repair drive is coming together nicely—people’ve been dropping off tools and supplies all morning. If you need anything checked on, I can swing by and ask around.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Oh, really? You’re sure it’s actually coming together and not just looking busy?

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Pretty sure, yeah — I saw stacks of boxes by the community hall and folks writing labels like they meant business. I can go take a closer look if you want the real scoop.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I’ll spread the word about the repair drive and make sure folks know what to bring.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Thanks, Vik — I really appreciate it. I’ll try to keep up and bring what I can.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Absolutely — I’ll keep reminding folks and make sure the details get around.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Sounds good — what’s the repair drive schedule?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: I’m not sure yet, but I’ll check while I’m out running errands and let you know.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Thanks — keep me posted when you find out.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I haven’t heard the details yet, but I’d like to know what needs fixing and how I can help.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: We’re still gathering the list, but we definitely need hands for patching up the shed and sorting donated supplies. If you’re free, I can point you to the first job when the crew meets.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That sounds good—I can help with either. Just point me to the first job when the crew meets.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can help coordinate around the school schedule for the repair drive—what time window are you thinking?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Thanks, Faye — that’d help a lot. I’m thinking a late afternoon window, maybe 3:30 to 5:30, so folks can swing by after pickup.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: That should work well — I’ll check the school pickup timing and see if we can keep the drive open in that 3:30 to 5:30 window.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I like a clear plan for the repair drive. Let’s set the time, the route, and who’s bringing what.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Yeah, that sounds good — let’s pick a time, map the route, and I can bring some supplies if you need.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Great — how about Saturday morning? If you bring the supplies, I’ll map the route and we can confirm who’s doing what.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: I’m going to spread the word about the repair drive and see who can help out. If you want, I can also invite a few more neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: That sounds helpful—just let me know the timing and where people should bring things. I’d rather keep it organized so we don’t end up with a pile of mismatched repairs.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Absolutely — I’ll send out the time and drop-off spot once I’ve got them, and I’ll ask folks to label what needs fixing so we keep it tidy.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I heard folks are organizing the repair drive, but I’m still catching up on the details. What’s the latest?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: We’re putting together a list of needed fixes and matching folks with jobs and supplies. If you want, I can fill you in and add your name where you’d like to help.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That’d be great—thank you. I’m happy to help where needed; just point me to the list and I’ll see what I can take on.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I want to make sure I’ve got the details right before I say yes—what exactly is needed for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: We’re collecting basic repair supplies like tape, screws, glue, and a few small tools so folks can fix up broken things at home. If you want, I can send the full list and drop-off details.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Yes, please send the full list and drop-off details so I can double-check everything before I decide.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can help with the repair drive, but I need to keep things quiet on my end.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Uli — I appreciate it. Keep it low-key, and I’ll handle the rest.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Thanks, Dane. I’ll keep my part quiet and be there when needed.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Sure thing, Mina — I can lend a hand and bring over any tools we need for the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Thanks, Gus — what time should I come by, and what tools do you want me to bring?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Come by around 9 tomorrow morning, and if you can bring a drill, a hammer, and a screwdriver set, that’d be great.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I don’t have anything logged about the repair drive yet—where are we starting from?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Let’s start with the basics: who needs repairs and what’s broken?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I don’t have any names or issues logged yet, so I need the first repair to note down. Tell me who needs help and what’s broken, and I’ll keep track.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Sure thing — I can lend a hand with tools for the repair drive. Just let me know what you need.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Thanks, Gus. I’ll let you know what tools we still need for the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Anytime, Rey — happy to help when you’re ready. Just send me the list and I’ll see what I can lend.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’m happy to help, but I’m a bit worried about the logistics—how many repairs are we talking about, and where would the drop-off be?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Good question — can you confirm how many repairs you can handle, and whether drop-off would be at your place or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I can probably handle a few repairs, but I’d need to keep it manageable. Drop-off at my place would be easiest, if that works.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: I’m happy to help spread the word about the repair drive—who should I check in with first?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Start with the block captains on Maple and Pine—they’ve been helping us coordinate. I’ll send you the flyer details right after this.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Great, I’ll check in with the Maple and Pine block captains first and keep an eye out for your flyer details.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I can check what supplies we’ve got on hand for the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Cleo — I’m running a little late as usual, but I can help once you’ve checked.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’ll take a quick look and let you know what’s missing.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, the repair drive? I heard it’s coming together nicely — folks are pitching in and the list of fixes is getting shorter by the day.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: That’s great to hear — I’ve been trying to keep track of the school pickup times around it, so I’m glad it’s moving along. If you hear what still needs doing, let me know.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Absolutely, I will — last I heard, it’s mostly a few odds and ends now. I’ll keep my ears open and tell you if anything major comes up.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Sounds good — what’s the plan for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: I’ll make a simple sign-up sheet, split the jobs by skill, and check in with everyone by Friday so we know what still needs fixing.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Nice, that sounds easy to follow. I can help get people signed up.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Sure thing, Leo — I’m happy to help with the repair drive. What do you need me to do?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Great — can you help sort the donated items and set them by category?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely — I can sort the donated items and set them by category.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: I heard the repair drive is coming up soon—want me to send you the details?

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Yes, please—I'd really appreciate that. I’m still catching up on the details.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Absolutely—I’ll send you the details right away, and I’ll keep an eye out for any updates too.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I’m keeping an eye on the repair drive location—where should I meet you?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Let’s meet at the community center front steps at 10:00. I’ll be there a few minutes early.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Perfect, I’ll meet you at the community center front steps at 10:00.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Did the repair drive already start, or are you still collecting donations?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I’m still checking the details, so I don’t want to guess. I can confirm whether the repair drive has started and how the donations are going.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Got it—please check and tell me whether it’s started and how the donations are going.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Sounds like a good idea—what’s the repair drive looking for right now?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Mostly tools, spare parts, and any small appliances that still have a little life in them. I’m trying to remember the exact list, but that’s the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Got it — I’ll keep an eye out for tools, parts, and any small appliances that still work. If I hear of anything, I’ll let you know.
